Right ankle fracture treated with casting in 2015

General anesthesia with Laryngeal Mask Airway (LMA), balanced technique with intravenous anesthetic agents and neuromuscular blockade

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr. Tan. I'm Dr. Lim from the anesthesia team. Today, we'll discuss your upcoming laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Let's start with your medical history. Can you tell me why you're having this surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Morning, doctor. Yeah, I've been having belly pains on the right side, especially after eating. The scans showed gallstones, so they said to remove the gallbladder.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Now, let's go through your medications. You're on amlodipine, atorvastatin, omeprazole, and metformin, correct? And I see metformin was stopped recently?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, doctor. I take amlodipine for blood pressure, atorvastatin for cholesterol, omeprazole for the acid reflux, and metformin for diabetes. But they told me to stop metformin a few days before surgery, right?

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Correct. We'll monitor your blood sugar closely. Now, about allergies—your records say 'no known allergies,' but I always double-check. Have you ever had any reactions to medications, especially antibiotics like penicillin?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Oh, wait a minute... I think I had a rash once when I took penicillin for a infection. It was years ago, but my skin turned all red and itchy. I told the doctor then, but maybe it wasn't recorded properly?

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for mentioning that. We'll note the penicillin allergy clearly. Even if it was a rash, we'll avoid penicillin and related antibiotics. Any other reactions to foods, latex, or other drugs?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, just that one time with penicillin. I don't think there's anything else.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Let's confirm your NPO status—have you had anything to eat or drink since midnight?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, doctor. My wife made sure I fasted properly. Just a bit of water with my morning meds, but that was hours ago.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Have you had anesthesia before? Any issues with previous surgeries or procedures?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Once, for a hernia repair. I woke up with a sore throat, but otherwise it was fine. No vomiting or anything bad.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Noted. Lastly, how's your overall fitness? Can you walk up stairs or do daily activities without excessive shortness of breath?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yeah, I walk to the MRT station daily. Climbing stairs is okay, though I get a bit tired if I rush. No chest pains or anything.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. We'll plan for general anesthesia with an LMA, as discussed. Your blood pressure and GERD will be managed carefully. Any questions for me?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, doctor. You've explained everything clearly. I'm ready to proceed.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Wonderful. We'll see you in the operating theater. Take care, and we'll ensure your safety throughout.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER

segments.speaker: PROVIDER

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] sixteen gauge peripheral IV placed

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] five hundred milliliters of lactated ringer's administered

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] mean arterial pressure dropped to fifty, phenylephrine one hundred micrograms bolus

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:20] heart rate increased to ninety, esmolol ten milligrams bolus

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Eh, still a bit groggy, but okay lah. Got some pain here at the tummy, you know?

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understandable. Can you rate the pain for me, like on a scale of 1 to 10?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe around 4 or 5? Not too bad, but I can feel it when I move.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Alright, we’ll manage that with some meds. Any nausea or feeling like you want to vomit?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No nausea, but my throat got a bit sore. Like something stuck there?

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That’s from the LMA tube during surgery. Should ease up soon. Breathing okay otherwise?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, breathing’s fine. Just a little discomfort when I cough.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Any memory of the operation itself? Sometimes people have bits they recall.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Nope, all black out. Woke up just now like that.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. Since you’ve got GERD, any acid reflux or chest discomfort post-op?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Not really. Stomach feels okay, just the usual tummy ache from surgery.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. We’ll keep an eye on your BP and lipids as usual. Any other concerns?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, all good. Thanks for checking on me.
